why: P279 is pure arithmetic over the hash-pinned P278 measurements, so the risks are different from P278: the rule is in-sample by construction, and the two things that can silently go wrong are (a) the banked input drifting under the analysis, and (b) the clustering code disagreeing with a from-scratch implementation. The record below pins both.

independent_recompute.estimator: union-find connected components over pairwise |a-b| <= 5 px edges, instead of the sorted-gap scan used by p279_consensus_cluster.py

perturbation_test.perturbation: one template disparity changed by +7 px in a copy of the banked raw file (breaks the frozen sha256)
perturbation_test.expected: hash gate fires -> overall INCONCLUSIVE, every prediction NOT SCORED

validity_clauses: fewer than two valid templates -> row non-evaluable, not a control
the banked input hash must match the value frozen in the pre-registration before any scoring
declared_weakness: P279-4 (random-template negative control) FAILED: random picking passed 10 of 11 controls, so the control cohort cannot discriminate aggregation rules and P279-2's no-regression result is weak evidence. The strong parts of P279 are the board's 0.2963 -> 0.0059 and the confirmed negative on the block. Fixed by P280, whose fresh-scene cohort is required to be discriminative (P280-3).
